findings.where: Article specimen, the run from the image caption through the subhead, the list and the PDF row (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The vertical rhythm breaks at every element the brief asked the specimen to prove. The subhead 'So, what are the key chapter topics?' sits almost against the caption above it and has more space below it, so it groups with the photo instead of the text it introduces (proximity). The three-item list is set nearly solid, its lines much closer together than the 30 px leading of the paragraphs around it. The PDF row follows the list with only a hairline and no breathing room.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for a rhythm that holds when Angélique adds an image, a caption, a list or a subhead. Angélique too: the first article she builds with these parts will look cramped and uneven. Mark's readers at the development banks will also object, because his long-form writing is the product and this makes it read as unfinished.

findings.where: Hero, the row of five outlined pills (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation) between the lead and the email action. On phone it wraps to three rows.
findings.fault: A row of five boxed, button-like shapes sits between the message and the one action. By similarity they read as five more things to press, kin to the outlined email button. They also push the action down to the bottom edge of the first screen. On phone the three rows of pills make the busiest part of the hero and put more distance between the heading and the address.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief and research call for one message and one action on the first screen. A development-bank officer scanning the hero also objects: they see six boxed controls where there is one way to reach Mark, and the address arrives last, at the fold.

findings.where: Hero, the giant ghost 'PPP' letters behind the heading (desktop). On phone they are cut off at the right edge beside the heading.
findings.fault: Pale display letters as tall as the heading sit right behind its first three lines, so the heading's figure fights a second figure of the same size in the same place (figure/ground). On phone the letters are cropped by the screen edge into unreadable fragments next to the text.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who wants one very large serif line with scale contrast, not more elements, and asked for restraint. Any visitor squinting at the hero also objects, because they see a muddy double layer where the line should stand clean.

findings.where: Phone hero, the order of photo, heading and action
findings.fault: On phone the square portrait and its caption fill almost all of the first screen, and Mark's line only starts near its bottom. The heading and the email action both fall below the first phone screen, so the first view shows a face and a nav with no message and no way to reach him.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency officer who opens the link on their phone and sees no sentence of Mark's and no contact without scrolling. The founder, who judges the first screen first and asks for one message and one action on it.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the blue panel on phone
findings.fault: On phone the sketch flips the hero's order, putting the portrait left and the text right. The heading is squeezed into a narrow column that breaks into lines of two or three words. It no longer previews the hero it stands for, which on phone stacks the photo above full-width text.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reads the motion sketch as a preview of how the hero enters. On phone it shows an arrangement the hero never uses.

findings.where: Style tiles below the fold (desktop): the Type pair row and the Texture column
findings.fault: The 'Source Sans 3' specimen on the right sits well below the 'Gelasio' specimen on the left, aligned to neither its baseline nor its top, so the pair does not read as a pair. The Texture column beside the palette leaves a tall empty block under its short note, and the motion column leaves another below 'Play again', so the two-column grid looks unevenly filled.
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing tiles side by side. The type pair is meant to be read across as two partners, and the misalignment makes the specimen sheet look less exact than the page it describes.
